Prevention: Avoid planting sudan grass, cotton and bermuda grass in the field as these are sources of infestations
Till the soil before transplanting to expose the eggs to predation and sun
Remove old crop debris and weeds in the family brassicaceae from the field before planting cabbage
Leave uncultivated patches within the field to encourage natural enemies (assassin bugs, solitary wasps, ants, preying mantids, spiders and parasitoids) breeding and multiplication
Monitoring: Scout for adult bugs as from 10.00h to 16.00h (mid-morning to late afternoon) when adult are generally most active in fields.
Monitor weekly for egg-laying sites on the leaves or in the soil
Look for adults that are 5-7 millimeters long, shield-shape, black with orange and white markings
Nymphs resemble adult but lack wings, orange-red colour and get darker as they moult into later instars
Check margins for stippling marks (engraved by dots) or small tan or white dots left where the leaves were pierced by insect
Take action when 10% of the crop is infested with the bugs
Direct Control: Hand pick adults and kill them early in the season
Spray soapy (teepol) water to wash off young bugs
ACHOOK 0.15% EC at 50 ml/20lts water every 14-28 days until no symptoms are seen
Spray pyrethroids such as lambda cyhalothrin concentrate such as
Karate® at 20g/20lts when the crop is established
Restrictions: Chemical control to start when adults/fresh feeding signs are observed on plant tissue
